messages:
jess: thinking about a hybrid RTB approach for spot GPUs — want to test capacity-optimized vs price-optimized bidding across regions. goal: reduce cost by ~18% without blowing tail-SLOs. thoughts? :thinking:
alex: sounds good. main risk is correlated evictions in a single region. we should force cross-region hedging + a small warm pool (3-5 nodes) in a dedicated reserve pool.
morgan: agree on warm pool. also can we bias bidding by instance-family? e.g., prefer A100s capacity-optimized, fall back to T4s price-optimized for low-priority work.
jess: yep. plan: primary pool = capacity-optimized A100 in us-west-2/us-east-1, secondary = price-optimized mixed (T4, A10) in us-east-2 and eu-west-1. use realtime bid thresholds and a soft-eviction grace (drain TTL 90s) to reduce cold-cache pain.
lei: what's our metric set for the experiment? eviction-rate, preemption duration, p99 tail latency, and effective $/GPU-hour? add failed-start rate for spot requests.
diego: add network egress variance — when we failover cross-region, egress cost spikes. also watch perf variance with different GPU types (FP16 perf differences).
jess: agreed on metrics. trying small-scale pilot next week (24h window), 50% traffic from the low-latency cohort, 50% best-effort. can we get a runbook for interruption handling?
alex: short runbook draft: 1) eviction event detected -> mark node unschedulable, drain workloads with grace 90s. 2) if KV-cache hotness > threshold, keep replica in warm pool until snapshot propagated. 3) fallback routing to dedicated/reserved pool if < 2 healthy replicas. 4) emit incident if >5% of requests hit fallback for >10m.
morgan: code snippet for spot request config (AWS-like) — share to experiment config: ```json
{"AllocationStrategy":"capacityOptimized","InstancePools":["p4d","p4de","a10g"],"OnDemandBaseCapacity":0}
```
lei: nice. we should also test aggressive price capping for non-SLO traffic. set max bid to 50% of on-demand for background jobs.
diego: to avoid correlated preempts, add randomized rebid jitter and small warmbuffer per zone (1-2 nodes) to absorb spikes.
sre-bot: meter: spot-eviction-count=12; avg-eviction-interval=18m; current-warmpool-size=3.
jess: thanks bot. one more ask: what about using mixed-signal bidding (capacity score * alpha + price score * (1-alpha)) and tune alpha? can we optimize alpha per region?
alex: yes, we can compute capacity-score using historical availability percentiles. run a grid search on alpha = [0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8] and look at cost vs p95 tail latency.
morgan: ops question — can we ensure rolling canary: start alpha=0.8 in one region, monitor fallback rate and tail latency for 2h, then expand.
lei: also add a cheap warm snapshot for KV-caches so new nodes can warm in <60s. that reduces user-visible regressions.
diego: reminder: track inter-region failover egress cost and latency delta; if egress cost > threshold, escalate to move more capacity into region.
sre-bot: note: scheduled test window next Tue 03:00-07:00 UTC. tagging owners: @jess @alex @morgan. :white_check_mark:
jess: perfect — i'll draft the experiment plan and post the A/B dashboard queries. thanks all :thumbsup:
